text:
maria: Heads up — we started seeing Xid 31s on a cohort of A100s in eu-west-1c around 2026-02-14 03:18 UTC. ~20 events across 6 hosts. Appears during low-latency RT traffic.

devin: Can you paste the /var/log/nvidia or kernel dmesg? Also which workloads?

maria: Logs show 'Xid (31) : a peer-to-peer or ASIC-level failure' intermittently. Using inference-runtime v1.8, model: redwood-lg-70b-8k qint8, batch_size usually 1 for RT, but we have an adaptive burst path where short sequences run on priority pool.

aj: Interesting — earlier Xid 31 we saw correlated with tiny sequences and high request spikes; was fixed by disabling CUDA peer-access on the host. Any PCIe errors? ECC counts?

maria: ECC counters clean; no ECC increment. PCIe RAS logs show occasional reset on pcie port 3. NVML shows GPU in-process list small. nvtop snapshots attached (can't attach in thread) here's the sample command we ran: ```nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu,fan.speed --format=csv```

jess: Are these hosts on a shared nodepool that runs both batch and RT? Might be noisy neighbors (nvlink traffic).

kai: I pulled job traces: the noisy time windows have synchronous small token generation loops (streaming) causing lots of short kernel launches. For A100, a specific driver combo 525.xx had a regressed behavior.

devin: Driver version?

maria: Driver 525.85.12. Kernel 5.15. Best reproducer when run the RT client with concurrency 60 short requests/s on a single GPU.

aj: We should triage sequence: 1) isolate to dedicated RT pool, 2) lower concurrency/pre-batch at inference runtime, 3) swap driver to 525.105.17 on canary host, 4) if persists, drain and replace GPU.

maria: I've kicked a canary host with 525.105.17 (host eu-w1c-034). So far 12h no Xid. Also reduced RT concurrency by 30% as temp mitigation.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled rolling driver canary to 3 hosts in eu-west-1c at 2026-02-14T06:00Z

jess: Cost tradeoff: replacing cards vs increasing spare pool vs forcing more batching. Spares are expensive; operators prefer driver swap + config changes first.

kai: Log correlation: Xid 31 events show consistent stack frames in our collector: kernel module nv-hostengine -> sm scheduler -> pci reset requested. I'll open an ML ticket with stacktrace.

maria: @aj @devin If canary stays clean for 48h we can promote driver and roll back batching change. If not, plan drain/replace for any host with >3 Xid31 in 24h.

aj: :thumbsup: agree. Add an alert rule: Xid31_count_by_host > 3 in 24h -> auto-schedule drain and tag host 'xid31-suspect'.

maria: Added alert to console, set auto-tag. I'll coordinate spare allocation with SRE.

devin: One more datapoint: latency percentiles jumped slightly during bursts even before Xid — makes sense. Also recommend adding nv-link and pcie counters to telemetry.

jess: :memo: I updated runbook with driver versions and mitigation steps.

maria: Thanks all. I'll post an incident summary if pattern holds.
